# Medical billing staffing cost: in-house vs outsourced vs remote staff

URL: https://medicalbillingteam.com/medical-billing-staffing-cost/

*Last reviewed: October 18, 2026.*

"How much does it cost?" is the first question practices ask about billing help, and the honest answer is: it depends on your volume, specialty and what you're comparing. Instead of quoting price ranges we can't back up, this guide shows you how to compare three common models using your own numbers and public wage data.

The three models:

1. **In-house staff** you hire and employ.
2. **Outsourced billing company** that runs billing for you.
3. **Dedicated remote staff** from a staffing provider, working in your systems.

For the bigger picture of roles and workflow, see our [revenue cycle management staffing guide](/revenue-cycle-management-staffing/).


## Model 1: In-house billing staff

### What you pay

Salary is the visible part. The full cost includes:

- **Wages.** The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports a May 2025 national median hourly wage of $23.32 for billing and posting clerks, with a mean annual wage of $51,070 ([BLS OEWS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ocwage.t01.htm)). For medical records specialists, the BLS category that includes medical coders, the May 2025 median was $51,140 per year ([BLS OOH](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/medical-records-and-health-information-technicians.htm)). Local wages vary widely, so check your metro area in BLS data.
- **Benefits and payroll taxes.** In private industry, benefits averaged 30.0% of total employer compensation costs in June 2026, and wages the other 70.0% ([BLS ECEC](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecec.nr0.htm)).
- **Recruiting and onboarding.** Job ads, interview time, background checks, training time before the person is productive.
- **Software and equipment.** Practice management seats, clearinghouse fees attributable to the user, computer, phone, workspace.
- **Supervision.** The hours a manager spends reviewing work and answering questions.

### What it's good for

Direct control, on-site collaboration with providers and front desk, and deep familiarity with your practice over time.

### Watch-outs

Single points of failure (one biller on vacation means nothing gets worked), recruiting difficulty, and turnover. In a 2025 vendor survey, 38% of billing professionals said they struggle to find qualified candidates and 28% cited rising wages they can't afford ([Tebra](https://www.tebra.com/theintake/getting-paid/medical-billing-pain-points-insights-solutions)).


## Model 2: Outsourced billing company

### How pricing usually works

Billing companies commonly charge:

- a **percentage of collections** (the most common model for practices);
- a **per-claim** fee; or
- a **flat monthly** fee, sometimes with minimums.

We don't publish typical percentages because we haven't found a reliable public source for them, and quotes vary with specialty, volume and scope. Get at least two written quotes and compare them on the same basis.

### Questions that change the real price

- What does "collections" include? Patient payments? Capitation? Refunds netted out?
- What is included: coding, credentialing, patient statements, patient calls, appeals, old A/R cleanup, reporting?
- Are there setup fees, minimum monthly fees or fees for old A/R?
- What are the contract term, termination notice and data return terms?
- Who owns the payer relationships and portal logins?

### What it's good for

Practices that want to hand off the whole function and don't want to manage billing staff at all.

### Watch-outs

Less day-to-day visibility, less control over priorities, and cost that rises with your collections even if the workload doesn't.


## Model 3: Dedicated remote billing staff

### How pricing usually works

Staffing providers typically charge a monthly or hourly rate per full-time staff member. You direct the work in your systems; the provider recruits, employs and supports the staff.

### Your costs on top of the rate

- **Management time** to assign work, review output and answer questions, especially in the first month.
- **Onboarding** on your procedures and payers.
- **Software seats** for each user.
- **Secure remote access**, such as a virtual desktop (VDI) or VPN with multi-factor authentication. See our [HIPAA guide](/hipaa-outsourced-medical-billing/) for what to require.

### What it's good for

Practices and billing companies that want dedicated capacity and control without local hiring, especially for queue-based work: eligibility, prior authorization, payment posting, A/R follow-up and denials.

### Watch-outs

You still own the process. If your workflows aren't documented, remote staff will struggle, just as a new local hire would. Time-zone coverage, payer contract restrictions on offshore access and HIPAA safeguards all need to be settled up front.


## A side-by-side comparison

| Factor | In-house | Outsourced billing company | Dedicated remote staff |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pricing basis | Wages + benefits + overhead | % of collections, per claim or flat | Per staff member (monthly/hourly) |
| Control of workflow | Full | Limited | Full (you direct) |
| Who manages staff | You | Vendor | You direct; provider employs/supports |
| Systems | Yours | Often vendor's or yours | Yours |
| Coverage for absences | You arrange | Vendor | Provider can backfill (confirm in contract) |
| Scales with | Headcount | Collections | Headcount |
| HIPAA arrangement | Workforce member | Business associate (BAA) | Business associate (BAA) |


## Worksheet: compare with your own numbers

1. **Monthly workload.** Claims per month, eligibility checks per day, authorizations per week, open A/R by aging bucket.
2. **Staff needed.** Roughly how many full-time people that workload requires (ask your billing lead).
3. **In-house cost per FTE.** Local wage × hours + benefits (BLS: benefits ≈ 30% of private-industry compensation costs) + recruiting, software, equipment, supervision ÷ 12.
4. **Outsourced cost.** Quoted percentage × average monthly collections + any minimums or add-on fees.
5. **Remote staff cost.** Quoted monthly rate × FTEs + your software seats + remote access + management time.
6. **Risk adjustments.** Cost of a vacancy month (unworked claims aging), turnover frequency, and the value of control and visibility to you.

The [Medical Billing Health Checklist](/checklist/) includes this worksheet in printable form.


## Hidden costs people forget

- **Vacancies.** When a biller leaves, A/R keeps aging. Some claims can hit timely filing limits; Medicare generally allows one calendar year from the date of service ([CMS Claims Processing Manual, Ch. 1](https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/guidance/manuals/downloads/clm104c01.pdf)) and many commercial payers allow less.
- **Owner time.** Physicians and managers who "just help with billing" are an expensive labor source.
- **Rework.** Denials that are corrected late cost more staff time than claims done right the first time. See [denial management basics](/denial-management/).
- **Switching costs.** Data migration, contract exit fees and retraining when you change models.


## Which model fits?

- **Choose in-house** if you have steady volume, can recruit locally and want everything on-site.
- **Choose an outsourced billing company** if you want to hand off the whole function and accept less control.
- **Choose dedicated remote staff** if you want control and dedicated capacity, have documented workflows, and can support secure remote access.

Many practices combine models: a local billing manager plus remote specialists for specific queues.

This site is operated by [Alliance Global Solutions](https://www.allianceglobalsolutions.com/), which provides remote staff; you can review its [service lines](https://www.allianceglobalsolutions.com/services/) on its own site. If you want help working through the worksheet, request a [free staffing assessment](/contact/). We'll tell you if another model makes more sense.


## FAQ

**How much does outsourced medical billing cost?**
Usually a percentage of collections, a per-claim fee or a monthly fee. Compare the fee applied to your actual collections against your fully loaded in-house cost.

**What is the fully loaded cost of an in-house biller?**
Wages plus taxes, benefits, leave, recruiting, training, software, equipment, workspace and supervision. Benefits averaged 30% of private-industry compensation costs in June 2026 (BLS).

**Are remote billing staff cheaper than in-house staff?**
Often the rate is lower, but compare total cost including your management time, onboarding, software and secure access.

**Is a percentage-of-collections fee better than paying for staff?**
It depends on volume and how much control you want.

**What hidden costs should I include?**
Vacancies, turnover, overtime, aging A/R, timely filing write-offs and owner time.

## FAQ

**How much does outsourced medical billing cost?**
Billing companies commonly price as a percentage of collections, a per-claim fee or a monthly fee. The right comparison is the fee applied to your actual collections and claim volume, compared with your fully loaded in-house cost. Ask exactly what services are included and how collections are defined.

**What is the fully loaded cost of an in-house medical biller?**
Wages plus payroll taxes, benefits, paid leave, recruiting, training, software licenses, equipment, workspace and supervision time. BLS data show benefits averaged 30% of private-industry employer compensation costs in June 2026, so salary alone understates the cost.

**Are remote medical billing staff cheaper than in-house staff?**
Often the hourly rate is lower, but you should compare total cost, including your management time, onboarding, software seats and secure remote access, against the fully loaded cost of a local hire for the same role.

**Is a percentage-of-collections fee better than paying for staff?**
It depends on your volume and needs. Percentage pricing scales with collections and bundles management, but you give up some control. Staffing pricing is predictable and keeps control in-house, but you manage the process.

**What hidden costs should I include?**
Vacancies and turnover, overtime, aging A/R while positions are unfilled, write-offs from missed timely filing limits, and the time owners or managers spend doing billing themselves.

# Medical billing for behavioral health practices and treatment centers

URL: https://medicalbillingteam.com/behavioral-health-billing/

*Last reviewed: October 18, 2026.*

Behavioral health billing looks simple from the outside: a lot of the same few codes. In practice, it's one of the more demanding specialties to bill well. Authorizations and concurrent reviews are frequent, benefits vary by level of care, many plans carve behavioral health out to a separate administrator, and substance use disorder (SUD) records carry their own federal privacy rules. This guide covers what's different and how practices and treatment centers staff the work. It's part of our [revenue cycle management staffing](/revenue-cycle-management-staffing/) series.


## Who this applies to

- Outpatient mental health practices: psychiatrists, psychologists, therapists, counselors and group practices
- Substance use disorder treatment centers across levels of care
- Intensive outpatient (IOP) and partial hospitalization (PHP) programs
- Residential treatment and detox programs
- Billing companies serving these providers


## What makes behavioral health billing different

### 1. Levels of care and benefits

Treatment centers bill across levels of care, each with its own benefits, authorization rules and documentation expectations. A patient's plan may cover residential care differently from IOP, with day limits or step-down requirements.

### 2. Authorizations and concurrent review

Many behavioral health services require prior authorization, and higher levels of care often require **concurrent review**: periodic clinical updates to the payer to continue authorized days. Missed reviews mean unpaid days. Staff need a tracker with review dates, approved days and the clinical contact for each case.

### 3. Carve-outs

A patient's medical plan may route behavioral health claims and authorizations to a separate behavioral health administrator with a different portal, payer ID and rules. Eligibility checks must identify the right entity.

### 4. Time-based and add-on codes

Psychotherapy codes are typically time-based, with add-on codes for things like interactive complexity or crisis services. Documentation must support the time and the service. Use current CPT guidance from the AMA ([AMA CPT overview](https://www.ama-assn.org/practice-management/cpt/cpt-overview-and-code-approval)) and payer policies; coders and billers should work from the current year's code set.

### 5. Privacy rules beyond HIPAA

- **Psychotherapy notes** receive special protection under the HIPAA Privacy Rule: most uses and disclosures require patient authorization ([HHS, Privacy Rule summary](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/laws-regulations/index.html)). Billing staff generally don't need them and shouldn't have access.
- **42 CFR Part 2** protects records of federally assisted SUD programs. It limits disclosures that would identify someone as having an SUD unless Part 2 permits it, allows a single patient consent for treatment, payment and health care operations, and restricts use of records in legal proceedings against patients. HHS notes the 2024 final rule's compliance date was February 16, 2026, and that some Part 2 requirements also apply to recipients such as HIPAA covered entities, business associates and qualified service organizations ([HHS, Part 2](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/hipaa-part-2/index.html)).

Make sure anyone touching Part 2 records, including billing staff, is trained on these rules and that your agreements cover them.


## The treatment center revenue cycle

### Admissions and VOB

The cycle starts before admission. VOB staff verify:

- active coverage and plan type;
- in- and out-of-network benefits by level of care;
- deductibles, coinsurance and out-of-pocket maximums;
- authorization and pre-certification requirements;
- day limits and step-down rules; and
- whether behavioral health is carved out.

Admissions staff need answers fast, often while a prospective patient is on the phone. Speed and accuracy both matter. See [eligibility verification and prior authorization](/eligibility-verification-prior-authorization/).

### Utilization review support

Clinical staff conduct reviews, but billing and UR coordinators track authorization numbers, approved days, next review dates and denials, and make sure authorization data flows onto claims.

### Claims, denials and A/R

Common problems include authorization mismatches (dates or units on the claim not matching the authorization), wrong payer (carve-out not identified), missing documentation for level-of-care billing and timely filing. Our guides on [denial management](/denial-management/) and [reducing A/R days](/reduce-ar-days/) apply directly.

### Payment posting and reconciliation

Out-of-network claims, single-case agreements and patient responsibility make posting more complex. Accurate posting shows whether payers paid what was agreed.


## Mental health parity

Federal mental health parity rules generally require that limits on mental health and substance use disorder benefits be no more restrictive than those on medical and surgical benefits. The parity regulations and their enforcement have changed in recent years, so check current guidance from the Departments of Labor, HHS and the Treasury. Billing staff don't enforce parity, but recognizing patterns of more restrictive treatment can inform appeals. For specific parity questions, consult counsel.


## Staffing behavioral health billing

### Roles

- **VOB / admissions support specialist**
- **Authorization and concurrent review coordinator**
- **Behavioral health biller / claims specialist**
- **A/R and denial follow-up specialist**
- **Payment poster**

### What to look for

- Experience with behavioral health payers, carve-outs and levels of care
- Comfort working with admissions under time pressure
- Accurate tracking habits for authorizations and review dates
- Training on HIPAA, psychotherapy notes and Part 2
- Clear documentation of every payer interaction

### In-house, outsourced or remote?

- **In-house** works well when admissions and billing need constant face-to-face coordination.
- **Outsourced billing companies** that specialize in behavioral health can take the whole function; confirm how they handle VOB speed and Part 2.
- **Dedicated remote staff** can cover VOB, authorizations, claims and A/R in your systems, including evening and weekend admissions coverage if scheduled. Put a BAA and access controls in place first, and limit access to what each role needs ([HIPAA guide](/hipaa-outsourced-medical-billing/)).

Our operator, [Alliance Global Solutions](https://www.allianceglobalsolutions.com/about-us/), provides remote staff including VOB and admissions support for treatment programs. If you're weighing options, request a [free staffing assessment](/contact/); we'll talk through your levels of care and payer mix. As always, please don't send patient information.


## Checklist for behavioral health billing leaders

- [ ] Authorization matrix by payer, level of care and service
- [ ] Concurrent review calendar with owner for each case
- [ ] Carve-out identification step in every eligibility check
- [ ] Psychotherapy notes excluded from billing staff access
- [ ] Part 2 consent tracking and staff training documented
- [ ] Authorization data validated against claims before submission
- [ ] Monthly denial review by payer and reason

A note on scope: this guide covers billing operations, not clinical or legal requirements. Licensure, program certification and state rules vary, so check them with your state agencies and counsel.



## FAQ

**Why is behavioral health billing different?**
Time-based codes, frequent authorizations and concurrent reviews, levels of care, carve-outs and Part 2 privacy rules.

**What is a VOB in a treatment center?**
A detailed benefits check by level of care, usually before admission.

**Does 42 CFR Part 2 apply to billing staff?**
Billing staff who handle Part 2 records must follow its rules. Compliance with the 2024 rule was required by February 16, 2026.

**Can remote staff handle admissions and VOB?**
Yes, with training, a BAA and appropriate access controls.

**What should I look for in behavioral health billing staff?**
Behavioral health payer experience, authorization tracking, carve-out knowledge, privacy training and strong documentation.

## FAQ

**Why is behavioral health billing different from other specialties?**
Behavioral health often involves time-based psychotherapy codes, frequent authorizations and concurrent reviews, levels of care with different benefits, carved-out behavioral health plans, and extra privacy rules for substance use disorder records under 42 CFR Part 2.

**What is a VOB in a treatment center?**
A verification of benefits confirms a prospective patient's coverage and benefits for specific levels of care, such as detox, residential, partial hospitalization or intensive outpatient, including authorization requirements, day limits and out-of-network benefits, usually before admission.

**Does 42 CFR Part 2 apply to billing staff?**
Part 2 applies to federally assisted SUD programs and to certain recipients of Part 2 records, including HIPAA covered entities and business associates and qualified service organizations. Billing staff who handle Part 2 records must follow its consent and redisclosure rules. HHS says compliance with the 2024 final rule was required by February 16, 2026.

**Can remote staff handle admissions and VOB for a treatment center?**
Yes, VOB and admissions support are phone- and portal-based and can be done remotely, provided staff are trained on levels of care, coverage rules and privacy requirements, and work under a BAA with appropriate access controls.

**What should a behavioral health practice look for in billing staff?**
Experience with behavioral health codes and payers, authorization and concurrent review tracking, knowledge of carve-out plans, understanding of Part 2 and psychotherapy notes rules, and strong documentation habits.

# How a remote medical billing team works

URL: https://medicalbillingteam.com/how-it-works/

A dedicated remote billing team is people, not software. Here is what the process looks like from the first conversation to day-to-day work.


## Step 1: Tell us about your workload

Use the [short form on the home page](/#assessment) or the [longer contact form](/contact/). We ask for practice-level details only: specialty, number of providers, a collections range and your current setup. **Never include patient information.**


## Step 2: Free staffing assessment

A billing staffing specialist talks with you, usually for 20 to 30 minutes, about:

- which queues are falling behind (eligibility, authorizations, claims, denials, A/R, posting);
- your systems, payers and specialty-specific rules;
- whether your systems can support secure remote access;
- the hours and coverage you need; and
- whether a remote team is a sensible fit at all.

If it isn't, for example because your processes are undocumented or your payer contracts restrict offshore access, we'll tell you.


## Step 3: Meet candidates, sign agreements, onboard

If you decide to go ahead:

1. **Role definition.** We agree on tasks, hours, systems and how performance will be measured.
2. **Candidate interviews.** You interview shortlisted candidates and choose who joins your team.
3. **Agreements.** A services agreement and a **business associate agreement (BAA)** are signed before anyone receives access to protected health information. See our [HIPAA guide](/hipaa-outsourced-medical-billing/).
4. **Secure access setup.** Unique logins, multi-factor authentication, role-based permissions and secure remote access (VDI or VPN), with no local downloads.
5. **Training on your workflows.** Your procedures, payers, escalation rules and reporting.
6. **Ramp-up.** Start with a defined queue, review work closely in the first weeks, then expand.


## Day to day

- Staff work your queues during agreed hours, often overlapping US business hours.
- You set priorities and approve anything outside the agreed rules (write-offs, refunds, appeals strategy).
- You get regular reporting on volumes worked and the KPIs you choose, such as days in A/R or denial rate. See [RCM KPIs, defined](/revenue-cycle-management-staffing/).
- You can add roles or reduce capacity under the terms of your agreement.


## What we don't do

- We don't ask for patient information through this website.
- We don't claim to be "HIPAA certified"; no such official certification exists.
- We don't promise specific outcomes before understanding your data.

[Request a free staffing assessment →](/contact/)

## FAQ

**Do remote staff use our software or theirs?**
Yours. Dedicated staff work in your practice management system, clearinghouse and payer portals, with access you grant and can revoke at any time.

**Who manages the remote staff day to day?**
You direct the work and set priorities. The staffing provider handles employment, HR, equipment, attendance and support, and can help with supervision and reporting.

**What do we need to have in place first?**
A signed business associate agreement, a secure way for staff to reach your systems (ideally a virtual desktop or VPN with MFA), user accounts with role-based access, and documented procedures for the tasks you're assigning.

**Can we start with one person?**
Yes. Many practices start with one role, such as eligibility verification or A/R follow-up, and add more once the workflow is running smoothly.

# Frequently asked questions

URL: https://medicalbillingteam.com/faq/

## About remote billing staff

**What is a remote medical billing team?**
Dedicated billing and revenue cycle staff who work remotely in your systems, under your workflows. You direct the work; a staffing provider recruits, employs and supports the staff. [How it works →](/how-it-works/)

**How is a staffing model different from outsourcing to a billing company?**
A billing company usually takes over the function, often for a percentage of collections. With staffing, you get dedicated people in your software and keep control. [Cost comparison →](/medical-billing-staffing-cost/)

**What roles can remote staff cover?**
Billing and claims, A/R follow-up, denial follow-up, eligibility/VOB, prior authorization, payment posting, coding (with credentials), credentialing and admissions or intake support. [RCM staffing guide →](/revenue-cycle-management-staffing/)

**Do you work with medical billing companies?**
Yes. The staffing provider usually acts as a subcontractor business associate and signs a BAA with the billing company.


## HIPAA and security

**Is anyone "HIPAA certified"?**
No. There is no official HIPAA certification, and HHS's Office for Civil Rights doesn't certify vendors ([HHS](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html)). Ask about specific safeguards. [HIPAA guide →](/hipaa-outsourced-medical-billing/)

**Will the staffing provider sign a BAA?**
A provider whose staff access PHI on your behalf is generally a business associate ([HHS](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/business-associates/index.html)), and a BAA should be signed before any access.

**Is offshore billing allowed under HIPAA?**
HIPAA has no offshore ban, but HHS notes added risk and enforceability concerns. Check payer and Medicaid contracts too.


## Cost and results

**How much does remote billing staff cost?**
Usually per staff member per month or hour. Use our [cost worksheet](/medical-billing-staffing-cost/) to compare models.

**Can you guarantee lower denials or fewer A/R days?**
No. Results depend on your payers, specialty, documentation and processes.


## Getting started

**What hours do remote staff work?**
Agreed up front, often overlapping US business hours.

**How long does it take to get started?**
It depends on role definition, interviews, agreements and access setup. The [assessment](/contact/) gives a realistic timeline.

**Can we start with one person?**
Yes. Start with one queue and expand.

No. Please do not include any patient information.

## FAQ

**What is a remote medical billing team?**
Dedicated billing and revenue cycle staff who work remotely in your systems, under your workflows. You direct the work; a staffing provider recruits, employs and supports the staff.

**How is a staffing model different from outsourcing to a billing company?**
A billing company usually takes over the billing function, often for a percentage of collections. With a staffing model you get dedicated people working your queues in your software, and you keep control of the process and payer relationships.

**What roles can remote staff cover?**
Common roles include billing and claims specialists, A/R follow-up, denial follow-up, eligibility and benefits verification (VOB), prior authorization, payment posting, coding (with credentials), credentialing and admissions or intake support.

**Do you work with medical billing companies?**
Yes. Billing companies often add dedicated remote staff as they take on new clients. In that case the staffing provider usually acts as a subcontractor business associate and signs a BAA with the billing company.

**Is anyone 'HIPAA certified'?**
No. There is no official HIPAA certification for companies or individuals. HHS's Office for Civil Rights does not endorse or certify vendors. Ask about specific safeguards instead: a BAA, MFA, secure remote access, role-based access, training and incident response.

**Will the staffing provider sign a business associate agreement?**
A provider whose staff will access protected health information on your behalf is generally a business associate, and a BAA should be signed before any access. Have your counsel review it.

**Is offshore billing allowed under HIPAA?**
HIPAA does not ban offshore work, but HHS notes that overseas arrangements can increase risk and raise enforceability questions. Address them in your risk analysis, and check payer and Medicaid contracts, some of which restrict offshore access.

**How much does remote billing staff cost?**
Pricing is usually per full-time staff member per month or per hour. Compare it with the fully loaded cost of a local hire and with billing company quotes using our cost worksheet. We don't publish generic price ranges.

**Can you guarantee lower denials or fewer A/R days?**
No. Results depend on your payers, specialty, documentation and processes. Anyone promising a specific reduction before reviewing your data should be asked how they can know that.

**What hours do remote staff work?**
Schedules are agreed up front. Many teams overlap US business hours so they can call payers and handle same-day eligibility work.

**How long does it take to get started?**
It depends on role definition, candidate interviews, agreements and access setup. The assessment call will give you a realistic timeline for your situation.

**Can we start with one person?**
Yes. Many practices start with one queue, such as eligibility or A/R follow-up, and expand once it runs smoothly.

**Who operates this website?**
This site is operated by Alliance Global Solutions, a provider of remote medical billing and revenue cycle staff. We may contact you about our services if you request it.

**Should I include patient details in my inquiry?**
No. Please do not include any patient information in forms, emails or chat. Practice-level details are all we need.

**How do I stop emails or calls?**
Use the unsubscribe link in any email, reply STOP to texts, or tell us on a call. We honor opt-out requests promptly.

# Medical Billing Health Checklist

URL: https://medicalbillingteam.com/checklist/

A one-page self-audit to find where your revenue cycle is leaking. Built for practice owners, office managers, billing managers and billing companies. It takes about 15 minutes and you don't need any patient data to complete it.

**Inside:**
- 43 yes/no checks across front end, claims, denials, A/R, payment posting, reporting, staffing and HIPAA
- A KPI worksheet with consistent definitions
- A simple staffing cost comparison worksheet


## How to use it

Answer each item **Yes**, **No** or **Not sure**. Every "No" or "Not sure" is a place to look first. This is a self-assessment, not an audit or legal review.


## 1. Front end: scheduling, eligibility and authorizations

- [ ] We verify eligibility and benefits before every visit, not just for new patients.
- [ ] We re-check insurance cards and demographics at every visit.
- [ ] We identify coordination of benefits (which plan is primary) before the visit.
- [ ] We maintain a current prior authorization matrix by payer and service.
- [ ] We track authorization expirations and visit limits.
- [ ] We give the front desk an estimated patient responsibility to collect at check-in.
- [ ] We identify behavioral health carve-outs during eligibility checks (if applicable).


## 2. Charges and claims

- [ ] Charges are entered within 1-2 business days of the date of service.
- [ ] Claims are scrubbed before submission.
- [ ] Clearinghouse and payer rejections are worked daily.
- [ ] We track timely filing limits for each major payer.
- [ ] Coding is done or reviewed by credentialed coders for our specialty.
- [ ] We updated our systems for this year's code changes (ICD-10-CM changes Oct 1; CPT/HCPCS changes Jan 1, plus quarterly updates).


## 3. Denials

- [ ] Every denial lands in one queue with a named owner.
- [ ] Denials are categorized by payer and reason.
- [ ] Denials are worked at least weekly, by deadline and dollar value.
- [ ] Appeals are tracked with deadlines and outcomes.
- [ ] Top preventable denial reasons are reviewed monthly and fed back to the front desk and coders.


## 4. Accounts receivable

- [ ] We calculate days in A/R the same way every month.
- [ ] We review A/R by aging bucket and by payer monthly.
- [ ] A/R follow-up is prioritized by dollar value and age, not alphabetically.
- [ ] Every touched claim has a documented action and next follow-up date.
- [ ] We have a written write-off policy with approval levels.
- [ ] Patient A/R has its own workflow (statements, reminders, payment plans).


## 5. Payment posting

- [ ] ERAs are posted daily and reconciled to bank deposits.
- [ ] Zero-pay and partial-pay lines are flagged as denials.
- [ ] We compare payments to contracted rates to catch underpayments.
- [ ] Secondary claims go out promptly after primary payment.
- [ ] Credit balances are reviewed and resolved regularly.


## 6. Reporting

- [ ] Leadership sees a monthly KPI report (see worksheet below).
- [ ] We can see each staff member's queue and output.
- [ ] We know our top 5 payers by A/R and by denials.


## 7. Staffing and coverage

- [ ] More than one person can do each critical billing task.
- [ ] Billing staff have protected time (they aren't constantly pulled to the front desk).
- [ ] Procedures for each queue are documented.
- [ ] We have a plan for vacations, leave and turnover.
- [ ] We've compared our fully loaded in-house cost with other options (see worksheet).


## 8. HIPAA safeguards for vendors and remote staff

- [ ] Every vendor or agency with PHI access has a signed BAA.
- [ ] Every user has a unique login with multi-factor authentication.
- [ ] Remote access uses a VPN or virtual desktop; local downloads are blocked.
- [ ] Access is role-based and removed the same day someone leaves.
- [ ] Our HIPAA risk analysis includes remote and offshore access.
- [ ] Vendors must notify us of incidents within a defined timeframe.

See the [HIPAA guide for outsourced billing staff](/hipaa-outsourced-medical-billing/) for the full question list.


## KPI worksheet

| KPI | Definition | This month | Last month | 3 months ago |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Days in A/R | Total A/R ÷ (charges for last 90 days ÷ 90) | | | |
| A/R over 90 days (%) | A/R aged 91+ days ÷ total A/R | | | |
| Denial rate | Denied claims ÷ claims submitted | | | |
| Clean claim rate | Claims accepted on first submission ÷ claims submitted | | | |
| Net collection rate | Payments ÷ (charges − contractual adjustments) | | | |
| First-pass resolution | Claims paid/resolved on first submission ÷ claims submitted | | | |
| Charge lag (days) | Average days from date of service to charge entry | | | |

Benchmarks vary by specialty and source; track your trend. Definitions are explained in our [RCM staffing guide](/revenue-cycle-management-staffing/).


## Staffing cost worksheet

| Line | In-house (per FTE) | Billing company | Remote staff (per FTE) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base cost | Wage × hours | Fee × monthly collections | Quoted rate |
| Benefits & taxes | (BLS: benefits ≈ 30% of private-industry compensation costs, June 2026) | Included | Included in rate (confirm) |
| Recruiting/training | | | |
| Software seats | | | |
| Equipment/remote access | | | |
| Management time | | | |
| **Monthly total** | | | |

Source for the benefits share: [BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecec.nr0.htm).


## Scoring

- **0-5 "No/Not sure":** solid foundation; focus on fine-tuning.
- **6-15:** specific gaps; pick the section with the most "No" answers and fix it first.
- **16+:** the revenue cycle likely needs more structure or capacity. Consider a [free staffing assessment](/contact/).

(Scoring bands are a simple rule of thumb, not a validated benchmark.)

# About this site

URL: https://medicalbillingteam.com/about/

Medical Billing Team is a resource for US medical practices and billing companies that are sorting out how to staff their billing and revenue cycle work. We write plain-English guides on topics like denial management, A/R follow-up, eligibility and prior authorization, HIPAA safeguards for outsourced staff and the real costs of different staffing models.


## Disclosure: who operates this site

**This site is operated by Alliance Global Solutions, a provider of remote medical billing and revenue cycle staff. We may contact you about our services if you request it.**

That means we have a commercial interest in the topics we write about. Alliance Global Solutions provides remote staff, based in the Philippines, for roles such as billing specialists, A/R follow-up, eligibility and insurance verification (VOB), prior authorization, payment posting, denial follow-up and admissions or intake support. You can learn more about the company on its own website: [about Alliance Global Solutions](https://www.allianceglobalsolutions.com/about-us/).

We think you should know that before you read anything here, so this disclosure also appears in the footer of every page and next to our forms.


## How we write our guides

- **We explain options fairly**, including when in-house staff or a full-service billing company is a better fit than remote staff.
- **We cite public sources.** Any statistic on this site links to a public source such as CMS, HHS, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the AMA or KFF. Where we cite a vendor survey, we say so. If we can't find a reliable public source for a number, we leave the number out.
- **We don't promise results.** Billing outcomes depend on your payers, specialty, documentation and processes. We don't claim that any staffing model will cut denials or A/R days by a set amount.
- **No fake proof.** You won't find invented testimonials, star ratings, client logos or case studies here. If we ever publish a client story, it will be real, permission-based and clearly labeled.
- **We are not "HIPAA certified," and neither is anyone else.** There is no official HIPAA certification. We explain what safeguards to look for in our [HIPAA guide](/hipaa-outsourced-medical-billing/).
- **We review and update.** Each guide shows a "last reviewed" date. Billing rules change, and we update pages when CMS, payers or code sets change.


## Not legal or financial advice

Our content is general information. It is not legal, compliance, coding or financial advice. For decisions about HIPAA, contracts or reimbursement, talk to qualified advisers.


## Your information

Our forms collect only business contact and practice-level information. **Please never submit patient information.** We explain what we collect and how we use it in our [Privacy Policy](/privacy/).


## Contact

Questions or corrections? [Contact us](/contact/). If you spot an error in a guide, we want to fix it.
